title: Switching Costs
coreMove: Compare the rival offer against the value the customer would lose or rebuild during migration.
sourcePressure: Switching costs come from customer value built up with the incumbent that would be destroyed or painfully rebuilt by leaving. The source includes financial, procedural, and relational costs and warns that repeat buying alone is not lock-in.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Switching costs mean loyalty, habit, repeat purchase, or disliking change.

sourceAnchors.name: Addiction
sourceAnchors.detail: the frozen table-of-contents subtitle signal for Switching Costs is Addiction, pointing to lock-in and accumulated continuity value
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Addiction is useful only as a signal: the customer stays because leaving destroys something already built, not because the old product is loved.
